correctness.rationale: The fast-x root X_q(y) is positive with uniform bounds m≤X≤M, giving forward quadrant invariance and global bounded trapping. The equilibrium condition reduces to quadratic qx²+(q+f−1)x−(1+f)=0, with exactly one positive root. On 0<q<1, use y=x(1−qx)/(x−1), X' =−(x−1)^2/D, h'=N/D where D=qx²−2qx+1>0. The sign threshold occurs at q0(x)=(x²−2x−1)/(2x(x²−x−1)) for x>1+√2, maximized at unique c>1+√2 solving c³−3c²−3c−1=0. The resultant gives 10q_*³+6q_*²+12q_*−1=0. Above q* one has h'≥0, strict negative divergence, positive equilibrium determinant and sink, so Poincaré–Bendixson and trapping prove global attraction and no cycles. Below it choose x=c, f=(1+c)(1−qc)/(c−1), s=1 and ω=−h'/2 to construct a hyperbolic source and trapping annulus, yielding a positive periodic orbit. Independent exact symbolic derivative and resultant checks reproduced q*=0.07973231434646405, c=3.847322101863..., and negative h'(c) for three subcritical q. The finite checks do not replace planar theorems.
